authors: Capliez, E., Ienco, D., Gaetano, R., Baghdadi, N. & Hadj Salah, A.
title: Temporal-domain adaptation for satellite image time-series land-cover mapping with adversarial learning and spatially aware self-training
relevance: The closest published method to our design: SpADANN transfers a land-cover classifier from one labelled YEAR to another over the SAME study area, combining adversarial alignment with spatially aware pseudo-labelling. Peer-reviewed, and it names the obstacle we hit - differing acquisition conditions between periods produce a distribution shift that plain transfer does not survive. Two limits to carry: it transfers to a SUCCESSIVE year (one step), not across 24 years and three sensors, and its engine is pseudo-labelling - the exact mechanism our finding 4 identifies as how the blind spot gets taught. The spatially aware part is the transferable idea; the iterated self-training is the part to be wary of.

title: Spatiotemporal masked pre-training for advancing crop mapping on satellite image time series with limited labels
source: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation 137, 104426
relevance: Peer-reviewed instance of the design Search 22 pointed at: pretrain on the unlabelled TIME SERIES itself, then fine-tune with few labels. Unlike the generic foundation-model papers, the pretraining corpus is the same archive the model is deployed on - which is precisely our 18 unlabelled years - so it is direct evidence that in-archive pretraining works in the limited-label regime rather than a claim transferred from a satellite benchmark. Caveat: crop mapping has strong seasonal periodicity our canopy series lacks, so the temporal structure it exploits may not exist for us.
